# Forecasting Results: LSTM vs Persistence

*Generated by `python main.py evaluate` on 2026-11-09 12:26. All numbers come from this run.*

## Set-up

- Data: Kolkata, 2018-06-16 to 2020-07-01 (see `reports/preprocessing_decisions.md`).
- Train up to 2019-09-30, validation to 2019-12-31, test after that.
- Inputs: previous 14 days of AQI, PM2.5, PM10, NO, NO2, NOx, NH3, CO, SO2, O3, Benzene, Toluene, doy_sin, doy_cos.
- Model: LSTM, 2 layers x 64 units, dropout 0.2; best epoch 33 of 53 (early stopping on validation loss); seed 42; device cpu.
- Baseline: persistence (tomorrow's AQI = today's AQI), scored on exactly the same days.

## Forecast error

| split | model | n | MAE | RMSE | MAPE_% | R2 | Bias |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| val | LSTM | 92 | 39.2 | 49.0 | 25.3 | 0.531 | 8.8 |
| val | Persistence | 92 | 32.4 | 45.2 | 20.9 | 0.601 | -2.7 |
| test | LSTM | 183 | 24.4 | 32.6 | 27.2 | 0.819 | 21.5 |
| test | Persistence | 183 | 20.5 | 31.4 | 17.2 | 0.833 | 1.3 |

- **Test MAE:** 24.4 vs 20.5 - LSTM is 3.8 higher (worse) AQI points than persistence.
- **Test RMSE:** 32.6 vs 31.4 - LSTM is 1.3 higher (worse).
- Validation MAE: 39.2 vs 32.4 - LSTM is 6.8 higher (worse).

## High-pollution alert (AQI > 200)

| split | model | actual_high_days | alerts_raised | correct_alerts_TP | false_alarms_FP | missed_FN | precision | recall | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| val | LSTM | 39 | 53 | 34 | 19 | 5 | 0.642 | 0.872 | 0.739 |
| val | Persistence | 39 | 38 | 29 | 9 | 10 | 0.763 | 0.744 | 0.753 |
| test | LSTM | 34 | 53 | 33 | 20 | 1 | 0.623 | 0.971 | 0.759 |
| test | Persistence | 34 | 35 | 23 | 12 | 11 | 0.657 | 0.676 | 0.667 |

## How to read these results honestly

- This is **one** training run, with **one** random seed, on **one** chronological split. A small difference between LSTM and persistence may not hold on other periods or seeds.
- The test period has only 183 days and 34 high-pollution days, so alert precision/recall can change a lot from a few days.
- The test period includes the COVID-19 lockdown (from 2020-03-25), when pollution patterns were unusual.
- These are associations learned from past data; they do not show what *causes* pollution.
